take_homes: Start from the teammate's job and its outcome, not from my agent. Then pick the smallest thing to share (context, skill, output or interface) that moves that outcome.
Sharing my agent file gets them a shell. The corrections and curated context are what make it work, and the shared context is what I can actually hand over.
If the people plan has no names, the rollout isn't built. Pick one person and ask what would make them switch from what they use now.

monday.move: Interview one pricing working group member about how they do the usage-pricing job today. Test one switch assumption, and see whether the pilot-cohort brief would land where they already look.
monday.who: One named person from the pricing working group. Which one is Monday's question.
monday.when: Monday, before the working group meeting
monday.stop_condition: They tell me the brief doesn't change how they do the job, or they already have a source they trust more.
monday.blocker: My team has no shared place for the context files, so the 'share the context' option has nowhere to live yet.

misconception.why: Corrections and curated context do the work, and the agent file only holds the instructions, so better prompts won't carry to my team. I'm not fully convinced prompts matter less for my own work.

one_line: The exercises are good and I came away with a Monday move. The lecture says the same thing about access and absorption four times, and I could have skipped half of it.
